title: ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

source.citation: Yao et al., ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models

core_question: How does interleaving generated reasoning text, task-specific actions, and environment observations perform on the tasks and configurations studied in this paper?
scope: The paper evaluates specific prompting and fine-tuning configurations on HotpotQA, FEVER, ALFWorld, and WebShop. Results are task-, model-, prompt-, and interface-specific; generated rationale is public model text, not verified source provenance or a faithful account of hidden reasoning.
key_ideas: The paper defines an interleaved trajectory of reasoning text, actions, and observations; the observation comes from the task environment.
Its knowledge tasks use a limited Wikipedia search/lookup/finish API; the authors also evaluate alternative routing and fine-tuning configurations.
Its reported results include both strengths and failure categories. They do not establish universal superiority, factuality, transfer, or controllability.
One ALFWorld appendix example edits text supplied to a later prompt and reports a changed trajectory; that single intervention does not establish general control.
